description: Ferrum Edge's closed error vocabularies: the granular ErrorClass (access-log error_class, ferrum_requests_total{error_class}, stream disconnect metrics) and the nine coarse client-facing X-Gateway-Error tokens. The header token is a stable contract and must not change spelling.

provenance.note: v0.9.17 adds loop_detected for the pre-routing proxy_hop_limit HTTP 508 fence; proxy_hops_invalid and route_protocol_admission map to no token. The closed header vocabulary has nine tokens, the reserved HTTP metrics vocabulary 25 labels, and ErrorClass 19 values. The hop fence emits status counters and bounded warnings, not a transaction summary or loop_detected metric row. Timeout descriptions clarify existing behavior: the backend handoff is marked immediately before send(), including connection setup, rather than after remote acceptance. Re-read at v0.9.19: the same nine tokens, 19 ErrorClass values and 25 reserved HTTP metric labels remain; no token-mapped phase is added. Transcribed connection_failure statuses widen from 502 to 502/504/503: connect timeouts answer 504 (Edge #6770), and pooled-transport DestinationRule maxConnections refusals answer 503 (Edge #6771), retaining their pre-wire class and token. The TLS meaning also includes typed setup errors without an underlying rustls source.

Transcribed HTTP-family dispatch-failure status mapping: ReadWriteTimeout answers 504; ConnectionTimeout also answers 504 (Edge #6770); BackendConnectionLimit answers 503 (Edge #6771); other classes answer 502. src/retry.rs retains connection_failure for pre-wire classes regardless of status.

surfaces.values: error_classes plus the tokens whose metric_label_without_error_class is true
surfaces.note: Omitted on 2xx, 3xx and 4xx. loop_detected is reserved; the hop-limit fence currently emits no error-class metric row.

error_classes.meaning: TCP connect did not complete before the configured timeout. Pre-wire HTTP connect timeouts answer 504 with connection_failure (Edge #6770 at v0.9.19), preserving connect-retry and target-rotation behavior. An established QUIC connection timing out while waiting on the backend also answers 504, but the dispatch records connection_error=false, so backend_timeout and status/method retry rules apply.

TCP connect refused (port not listening, firewall RST), including connect-phase RSTs. A TLS handshake failure after TCP connect is not this class. One carrying a typed rustls error is tls_error when the gateway independently knew it was still setting up, and otherwise connection_reset (issue #4536); a backend mTLS rejection that reqwest surfaces only as a canceled request is connection_pool_error (issue #4406).

RST received after the connection was established and, for TLS, after the handshake completed. Also the verdict for an ambiguous post-connect failure with no independent setup-phase evidence (issue #4536).
Peer sent FIN before the response completed; broken pipe; aborted connection; post-connect UnexpectedEof or an incomplete (truncated) HTTP message.
The backend hostname could not be resolved.

TLS or DTLS handshake failed with independently established setup-phase evidence: a caller observing a typed rustls error while it knows it is dialing or handshaking, or a typed setup error such as StreamSetupKind::BackendDtlsHandshake even without an underlying source. Without setup-phase evidence a typed rustls error is connection_reset. A missing close_notify is teardown, not this class.

A backend read or write exceeded its per-direction timeout. From v0.9.14 this includes a timeout that reqwest reports while the buffered collector reads a larger or limited response body (504; earlier releases labelled such reqwest-reported read errors response_body_too_large). The collector's own idle backend_read_timeout_ms timeout was already read_write_timeout.

A client-side, backend-health-neutral terminal: client departure, malformed or stalled upload, client RPC deadline, or authorization expiry. This class alone does not prove client departure. Only a typed proven client abort justifies the 499 log/metric terminal (native gRPC CANCELLED under HTTP 200); other terminals retain their own statuses. After response headers are committed, the committed HTTP status stands.
error_classes.x_gateway_error_note: Only when the public status is 5xx.

error_classes.meaning: HTTP/2 or HTTP/3 protocol error after a stream opened (stream reset, GOAWAY, RST_STREAM), or an RFC 6455 WebSocket protocol violation. From v0.9.14 a backend HTTP/2 RST_STREAM or GOAWAY with any reason except NO_ERROR, before the response headers, during a buffered body read or while a body streams, is this class and is charged to the target's circuit breaker and passive health; a reset the gateway raises itself keeps its previous class.
The backend response exceeded the configured maximum size. From v0.9.14 other read errors in the buffered collector report their real class instead of this one.

The process-wide retained-response budget (FERRUM_RESPONSE_BUFFER_MAX_TOTAL_BYTES) could not admit this response. Gateway-local and transient; non-retryable and neutral to backend health; HTTP 503 or gRPC RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED.
The request body exceeded the configured maximum size.
Could not acquire or create an HTTP client from the pool, including a hyper is_canceled() request that was never dispatched (issues #3578, #4406).
EADDRNOTAVAIL: all ephemeral ports are in use.
The peer closed the session cleanly: HTTP/3 H3_NO_ERROR or GOAWAY at the response read boundary, or a WebSocket Close frame.

Terminal gateway policy decision: pre-dial egress or SNI policy, opaque-TLS SNI admission refusal, admission overflow, final request-body hook rejection, or response-transformer output above the response ceiling. Non-retryable and neutral to backend health.

x_gateway_error_overrides.when: Response-transformer output above the effective response ceiling (HTTP 502).
Route-deadline 504 whose recorded phase is before_dispatch or retry_backoff: no backend held the request.

error_classes.meaning: The gateway refused to open a new backend connection because the destination is at its DestinationRule connectionPool.tcp.maxConnections ceiling. HTTP-family terminal refusals answer 503 (Edge #6771 at v0.9.19); pooled transports retain connection_failure. Native gRPC uses UNAVAILABLE under HTTP 200. The reqwest/HTTP-1.1 and WebSocket lanes also answer 503 but use DispatchPolicyRejected because they do not rotate. Pre-wire and neutral to backend health.
An accepted gateway trust publication withdrew an authority, so a gateway-to-mesh TLS transport was refused (issue #3859). Pre-wire and neutral to backend health.
Catch-all for unclassified gateway-side rejections and unknown failure modes.

x_gateway_error_tokens.meaning: Pre-wire connect-refused, DNS, TLS or pool failure (502), connect timeout (504; Edge #6770), or a pooled-transport (direct H2, native H3, HBONE, sidecar mTLS) DestinationRule maxConnections refusal before dialing (503; Edge #6771). Also the token for every ErrorClass whose request_reached_wire is false.

Backend dispatch did not answer before its deadline (504). A route-total deadline is a backend timeout once send() begins, including TCP/TLS connection establishment; remote acceptance or receipt of request bytes is not implied. This clarifies existing behavior.
The backend returned a 5xx, or a post-wire 5xx had no more specific token. Also the metric label for an unclassified backend 5xx. Never used for a response that did not reach a backend.
The circuit breaker for the backend was open; the request never reached a backend.
Gateway resource refusal: overload or drain reject_new_requests (503), or response-transformer output above the configured response ceiling (502).

A matched route rule's total request deadline (mesh_route_dispatch request_timeout_ms, Gateway API timeouts.request) expired before backend dispatch began: client upload, a gateway-local phase, admission, or retry backoff (504). The route timeout phase is before_dispatch or retry_backoff. Introduced in v0.9.8; v0.9.17 clarifies existing behavior.

The received X-Ferrum-Hops count reached FERRUM_MAX_PROXY_HOPS; the gateway refuses before routing and contacts no backend. Only the refusing hop writes this token; an outer gateway relaying 508 uses backend_error. HTTP 508 is never retried, regardless of retryable_status_codes. Native gRPC returns trailers-only FAILED_PRECONDITION with no HTTP 5xx token; malformed hop fields return 400 or native gRPC INVALID_ARGUMENT with no token. The metrics label is reserved: this fence currently emits no transaction summary/error-class metric row.
